Silent Beauty of Sundarban2013 — Acrylic on canvas, 30 × 36 in
"My artistic practice investigates the emotional and spiritual relationship between people, nature, and cultural memory."

Through colour, texture, and abstraction, Pritom transforms ordinary experiences into visual narratives that encourage reflection and dialogue — each painting a journey between reality and imagination, celebrating resilience, identity, and shared humanity. Working primarily in acrylic on canvas and watercolour on paper, he draws on riverine environments, rural life, bird habitats, and the ecological character of Bangladesh.

About the Artist

Twenty years between
river and canvas

Hasan Ferdous Pritom is a Bangladeshi visual artist whose practice explores the emotional and spiritual relationships connecting people, landscape, and cultural memory. Working primarily in acrylic on canvas and watercolour on paper, he draws upon riverine environments, rural life, bird habitats, and the ecological character of Bangladesh.

Through layered colour, atmospheric space, texture, and semi-abstract forms, he transforms familiar natural scenes into reflective visual narratives. He is currently pursuing a PhD in Fine Arts at the Faculty of Fine Art, University of Dhaka.
